note: Three axes: technical domain x role function x organizational context. Job titles are aliases for combinations, and none of the axes produces a ranking. This file is where changes are made. The eight axes, two scales and four levels use the same values as the Mechanical Engineering Core: results from two majors can only be compared on the same ruler, and building a new ruler for each major would break comparison within a university

J1.name: Problem definition
J1.question: Who decided what to work on?

J2.name: Requirements interpretation
J2.question: Did you turn the requirements into numbers and constraints?

J3.name: Technical decisions
J3.question: Which items did you decide yourself?

J4.name: Methods and tools
J4.question: What did you use, and how?

J6.name: Comparison and verification
J6.question: What did you compare it against?

J7.name: Failure and correction
J7.question: How did you narrow down what went wrong?

J8.name: Organizational use
J8.question: Who used it, and for what?

S4.note: Screening scale. The four axes asked at BASIC. Organizational use is left out of screening because it puts undergraduates at a structural disadvantage: whether your work was used by an organization can only be answered if you were placed in one, and someone who has only done classes and a capstone will have that cell empty even if they made decisions. Organizational use is asked only in the in-depth stage

S8.note: Full scale. STANDARD and above. Do not use S8 as the denominator for S4. What the in-depth stage newly opens are the four axes not in screening (problem definition, requirements interpretation, methods and tools, organizational use)

levels.L1: Exposed. Watched or reused what someone else did
levels.L3: Owned. Decided it myself, and the result was used

technical_domains.name: Policy and Program Planning
technical_domains.owns: Decides where to use budget and staff and where not to use them

technical_domains.name: Interpreting Laws and Regulations
technical_domains.owns: Decides which provisions to apply and which not to apply
subareas: Finding the provisions that are the basis

technical_domains.name: Budget Planning and Spending
technical_domains.owns: Decides how much to give each program and how that money will be spent

technical_domains.name: Administrative Procedures and Civil Complaints
technical_domains.owns: Decides how to finish each application within the deadline and with what result

technical_domains.name: Human Resources and Organization Management
technical_domains.owns: Decides how many people to put in which position and how to evaluate them

technical_domains.name: Performance Management and Evaluation
technical_domains.owns: Decides what to count as results and how to judge them

technical_domains.name: Public Data and Statistical Analysis
technical_domains.owns: Decides what to count from accumulated data and how, to use as a basis for decisions

technical_domains.name: Accounting and Audit
technical_domains.owns: Judges whether money spent fits the rules and the proof, and decides the range of findings

technical_domains.name: Resident Participation and Cooperation
technical_domains.owns: Decides whose opinions to receive, by what method, and how far to reflect them

technical_domains.name: Disaster and Safety Management
technical_domains.owns: Decides which dangers to look at first and what to do at which step

technical_domains.name: Public Program Management and Procurement
technical_domains.owns: Decides what to give out and how, and whether to accept the delivered results

technical_domains.name: Digital Administration and Information Disclosure
technical_domains.owns: Turns work into tasks for a system and decides how much to make public

role_functions.name: Policy and Program Planning
role_functions.output_kind: Program plan · Performance indicator table · Schedule
role_functions.success: One plan that fits the budget and staff and can be checked with indicators

role_functions.name: Analysis and Estimation
role_functions.one_line: Looks ahead with numbers before a decision
role_functions.output_kind: Demand estimate · Fiscal needs estimate · Statistical analysis report
role_functions.success: A basis that matches the results and changed a decision

role_functions.name: Review and Audit
role_functions.one_line: Checks whether what was done is right
role_functions.output_kind: Review opinion · Inspection report · Settlement review results
role_functions.success: A result where the provisions and proof match and the covered scope is written down

role_functions.name: Implementation and Operations
role_functions.one_line: Keeps work running again and again
role_functions.output_kind: Work handling procedure · Spending records · Delegation of authority criteria
role_functions.success: The same application gives the same result, and it can be reversed

role_functions.name: Civil Complaints and Field Response
role_functions.output_kind: Service criteria · Handling deadline management · On-site action records
role_functions.success: Within the set deadline, and the same civil complaint does not come back

role_functions.name: Consultation and Coordination
role_functions.one_line: Brings the decisions of several institutions together into one
role_functions.output_kind: Consultation materials · Agreed terms · Change records
role_functions.success: Rate of meeting consultation terms, and deadlines

role_functions.name: Survey and Research
role_functions.one_line: Narrows down things that have no answer yet
role_functions.output_kind: Research design · Fact-finding survey report · Pilot program results
role_functions.success: The question is narrowed and a method remains

role_functions.name: Systems and Personnel Management
role_functions.one_line: Makes sure standards are kept all the time
role_functions.output_kind: Job criteria · Evaluation criteria · Rule revision records
role_functions.success: The same problem does not come back, and the basis of decisions can be traced

role_functions_note: There are eight, and they use **the same codes** as the Mechanical Engineering Core. Role functions are a layer above the major, so they are not created again for each major. All names were changed into public administration terms: `Design and Development` and `Process and Mass Production` are words for making things, so a student who writes policy or receives civil complaints cannot find their place. The meaning of the work is kept the same, so the axes do not split; what differs is the kind of output: program plans, decision records and settlement data take the place of drawings

org_contexts.name: Central Government Agencies
org_contexts.performance: Policy goal achievement · Revision of laws · Responses to the National Assembly and audits
org_contexts.differs: The standards I write apply in the same way across the country

org_contexts.name: Local Governments
org_contexts.performance: What residents feel · Spending rate · Responses to the local council and audits
org_contexts.differs: You meet the same residents again and again, and reactions from the field come back right away

org_contexts.name: Public Institutions and Public Corporations
org_contexts.performance: Program goal achievement · Management evaluation · Safety and quality
org_contexts.differs: Looks at program results and public value together

org_contexts.name: Education and Research Institutions
org_contexts.performance: Project performance · Report quality · Policy contribution
org_contexts.differs: You must show on your own that the method is valid

org_contexts.name: Regulatory and Supervisory Agencies
org_contexts.performance: Judging whether standards are met · Review handling · Responses to appeals
org_contexts.differs: The traceability of the judgment is the output

org_contexts.name: Nonprofit and Civil Society Organizations
org_contexts.performance: Program performance · Settlement of donations and subsidies · Changes in target groups
org_contexts.differs: Finds ways to reach the field with few resources

org_contexts.name: Private Contractors and Service Providers
org_contexts.performance: Contract performance · Meeting deadlines · Client evaluation
org_contexts.differs: The needs of one client set the standard

boundaries.a_difference: Separates what to do from what not to do
boundaries.b_difference: Decides how much to give that work
boundaries.a_question: Have you chosen yourself and written down the programs not to do this time?
boundaries.b_question: Have you divided yourself the amount for each program and kept the basis?

boundaries.pair: Interpreting Laws vs Handling Civil Complaints
boundaries.a_difference: Separates the scope of application and the exceptions of provisions
boundaries.b_difference: Finishes one application on the spot within the deadline
boundaries.a_question: Have you divided yourself the provisions to apply and the provisions not to apply?
boundaries.b_question: Have you judged a received case yourself and handled it or asked for more documents?

boundaries.a_difference: Judges whether it fits the rules and the proof
boundaries.b_difference: Judges whether it reached the goal and why
boundaries.a_question: Have you chosen yourself the samples and period and checked them?
boundaries.b_question: Have you set yourself the indicators for what to count as results?

boundaries.pair: Public Data Analysis vs Performance Evaluation
boundaries.shared: Builds a basis for decisions with numbers
boundaries.a_difference: Extracts indicators from data and compares them
boundaries.b_difference: Judges program achievement with those indicators
boundaries.a_question: Have you defined an indicator and extracted it from data yourself?
boundaries.b_question: Have you set yourself the criteria for judging achievement?

boundaries.pair: Procurement and Contracts vs Program Supervision
boundaries.shared: Handles work given to outside parties
boundaries.a_difference: Writes what to give out and by what method
boundaries.b_difference: Judges whether to accept the results brought back
boundaries.a_question: Have you written yourself the scope of work and the ordering method?
boundaries.b_question: Have you judged yourself whether delivered items met the scope of work?

boundaries.shared: Prevents accidents or keeps them from growing
boundaries.a_difference: Runs the steps and roles when something happens
boundaries.b_difference: Finds violations of standards before something happens and has them fixed
boundaries.a_question: Have you set yourself the response steps and the division of roles?
boundaries.b_question: Have you set yourself the inspection targets and the range of correction requests?

boundaries.a_difference: Receives opinions and reflects them in decisions
boundaries.b_difference: Announces what has been decided and reduces misunderstanding
boundaries.a_question: Have you designed yourself whose opinions to receive and by what method?
boundaries.b_question: Have you chosen yourself what to announce, when, and in what words?

boundaries.a_difference: Turns workflows into tasks for a system
boundaries.b_difference: Decides how much to make public
boundaries.a_question: Have you turned current forms and workflows into a list of features?
boundaries.b_question: Have you divided yourself the range to disclose and the range to hide?

boundaries.a_difference: Sets criteria and runs things by those criteria
boundaries.b_difference: Researches whether the current placement fits and narrows down problems
boundaries.a_question: Have you set job criteria or evaluation criteria yourself?
boundaries.b_question: Have you researched the current workload and placement and narrowed down the positions that do not fit?

boundaries.pair: Policy Planning vs Survey and Research
boundaries.shared: Builds the basis for what to do
boundaries.a_difference: Confirms a plan within the available resources
boundaries.b_difference: Narrows down what is not yet known and builds an answer
boundaries.a_question: Have you confirmed yourself one plan that fits within the resources?
boundaries.b_question: Have you designed a survey yourself, deciding what to ask and what to find out?
